stem: Which combination of tissues is required to obliterate the interventricular foramen?

options.text: Ventricular septum, endocardial cushions, and the spiral aortic septum
Septum primum, septum secundum, and the foramen ovale
Arterial trunks and the venous channels
The fourth aortic arch and the sixth aortic arch

explanation: Closure of this opening requires contributions from the muscular septum, the central cushions, and the descending spiral septum.
rationale: Identify the three distinct regions that meet to separate the right and left pumping chambers.

optionExplanations.A: Closure of this opening requires contributions from the muscular septum, the central cushions, and the descending spiral septum.
optionExplanations.B: These structures are exclusive to the partitioning of the atria, not the ventricles.
optionExplanations.C: These are the external anchoring points of the heart tube rather than internal partitioning tissues.
optionExplanations.D: While they form the great vessels, they do not participate in closing the hole between the ventricles.

source.hint: Identify the three distinct regions that meet to separate the right and left pumping chambers.
